key_insight: Cold relaxes process quality: thermal SRH leakage essentially vanishes at 77 K, so crude low-mask poly-Si TFTs on glass could hold charge if their leakage were thermal.
killer_doubt: Grain-boundary leakage is trap-assisted and field-enhanced, so it likely falls ~1e2-1e3x, not 1e6. LN2 adds ~10-15 W at the wall per W, with no density gain.
decisive_experiment: In a university fab, build SPC poly-Si TFTs with 10 fF MIM caps. Measure off-current and retention from 300 K to 77 K at Vds 0.1-1.5 V on 200 devices. Under $50k.
prior_art: Rambus/Microsoft cryo-DRAM (2017); SNU CryoRAM (ISCA 2019); Phase B N-94 77 K oxide gain cell; R07 I-06479 150 K poly-Si (DROP).

key_insight: Package-level harvest frees dies from the DIMM form factor for CXL cards. DRAM has no dominant wear-out, so second life is physically sound and needs no wafers.
killer_doubt: Already shipping: GreenSKU and Structera X reuse DDR4 over CXL. Reflow and reball add fallout risk, the DDR4 pool is one-time, and CXL adds ~70-100 ns.
decisive_experiment: Desolder, reball and retest 1,000 retired DDR4 packages. Compare fallout, retention tail and row-hammer threshold against the same lot left on DIMMs. Under $100k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; R16 I-00224 (HOLD, the canonical reuse review); R26 I-06854 phone LPDDR desolder-to-CXL (ADVANCE).

key_insight: Measured per-DIMM timing and refresh bins written into the SPD, plus a warranty, form the trust layer that makes grey-market DIMMs an enterprise product.
killer_doubt: ITAD resellers already sell tested hyperscale DIMMs. The supply is one-time (DDR4 is end-of-life) and needs DDR4-capable CXL controllers that add ~70-100 ns.
decisive_experiment: Profile 500 retired DIMMs on FPGA rigs and rewrite their SPD bins. Track corrected and uncorrected errors in a CXL pool for 6 months against unbinned controls. Under $150k.
prior_art: ITRenew/Iron Mountain recertified hyperscale hardware; R27 I-08260 signed-certificate tester (HOLD); REAPER retention profiling; Microsoft GreenSKU.

key_insight: The first-principles premise holds: a five-year-old DRAM die is nearly as good as new, so recovered bits arrive in months rather than fab-years.
killer_doubt: Same mechanism as I-04852 and R16 I-00224. R16 put retiring DDR4 at ~5-7 EB/yr (~15% of bit output), but resale channels and CXL controllers already capture it.
decisive_experiment: Covered by I-04852: measure desolder/reball fallout and the retention tail on 1,000 harvested packages against controls left on DIMMs. Under $100k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; ITRenew/Iron Mountain resale; R16 I-00224 and I-10802.

key_insight: A Gen-8.5 panel has the area of ~78 wafers on depreciated tools. Multi-tier oxide gain cells need no Czochralski silicon, quartz crucible, HAR etch or EUV.
killer_doubt: The economics need F~0.5 um. FPD steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um, which gives ~$13/GB (R17), worse than DDR5's $1.48/GB cost, and 16-tier panel CMP is unproven.
decisive_experiment: Pair with I-07130: on Gen-2 glass, pattern a 4-tier IGZO 2T0C array at ~0.5 um with IL for the array layers. Measure tier yield per cm2, Vt sigma and 85 C retention. ~$500k.
prior_art: Same core as R17 I-10785 (ADVANCE, merge into it); R01 I-04673; SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM; PragmatIC FlexIC; Phase B N-36, N-38.

key_insight: Ramp months burn depreciation. Transferring defect-classifier knowledge without moving raw data could shorten a new line's learning curve.
killer_doubt: Yield learning is recipe- and tool-specific and is the firms' crown-jewel IP. Three makers hold ~90% of DRAM and won't contribute, so the library fills with logic data.
decisive_experiment: Train a federated wafer-map classifier on public sets (WM-811K, MixedWM38) plus one pilot-line partner. Measure accuracy on a held-out fab against local-only training. Under $200k.
prior_art: Federated wafer-map defect classification papers (2021-24); PDF Solutions Exensio; KLA Klarity; CHIPS SMART USA digital-twin institute [training knowledge].

key_insight: Lines are already EUV-free via SAQP. The prize is 3-beam hexagonal IL for honeycomb capacitor and landing-pad holes (DRAM's hardest layers), and sub-um array layers on display glass.
killer_doubt: Rigid fringes cannot follow distortion. DRAM needs ~2-3 nm overlay, and glass at ~3 ppm/K moves ~0.8 um across 2.5 m per 0.1 K, so scanning, phase-corrected IL is required.
decisive_experiment: On a university IL bench, print hexagonal hole arrays and double them by SADP. Align a DUV cut mask to a scanner-printed prior layer and measure CDU, LER and overlay. ~$300k.
prior_art: Phase B N-32; Intel/Borodovsky complementary lithography with Multibeam e-beam cuts; Eulitha Talbot lithography; MIT SBIL. IL for DRAM holes: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: In 4F2 VCT DRAM, the access-transistor step can also build per-segment gain devices. 16-cell local lines cut Cs ~5x and capacitor AR from ~70:1 to ~15:1 with no added mask.
killer_doubt: Charge sharing stays destructive, so segments need write-back and precharge. IBM used 3T per 32 cells (~20% area at 16), and ~40 mV Vt sigma leaves ~6 sigma.
decisive_experiment: Tape out a 28-65 nm MPW with 16-cell local lines, 0.5-2 fF cells and 2-3T local amplifiers. Map read BER against Cs and global swing, and add VCT Vt-mismatch TCAD. ~$300k.
prior_art: IBM eDRAM 3T micro sense amp, ~32 cells per local bitline (Barth, ISSCC 2007/JSSC 2008, via search snippet); Phase B N-04, N-48; R23 I-05154.

key_insight: Moving the deepest etch into a shared, fully used substrate fab is sound capital logic. Trench-first matches IBM's flow order, so FEOL on top is thermally plausible.
killer_doubt: Density stays at eDRAM level: a ~0.026 um2 22 nm DT cell is ~20x 1b DRAM's area per bit. Logic must also adopt the substrate's fixed grid and buried-strap module.
decisive_experiment: Etch trench-capacitor coupons, run a 130-180 nm FEOL on top at a U.S. foundry, and measure capacitor leakage, strap resistance and Cs after the full thermal budget. ~$600k.
prior_art: IBM/GlobalFoundries deep-trench eDRAM (POWER7-9); Murata/IPDiA and TSMC deep-trench silicon capacitors; Soitec engineered substrates; R07 I-04623 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Few-electron storage needs only thin films and one shared vertical-gate hole, so tiers are cheap depositions. Write-verify can absorb part of the grain scatter.
killer_doubt: Few-electron windows sit near RTN and grain scatter, and 3x majority triples area. Tunnel writes need >=3e8 cycles (C0-1), not shown. Grain-limited strings read at nA, i.e. us sensing.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate poly-Si nanowire grain cells in a university fab. On 1,000 devices, measure the post-write-verify Vt window and sigma, 85 C retention and endurance to 1e10 cycles. ~$150k.
prior_art: Yano et al., Hitachi single-electron memory (128 Mb prototype, 1998); Tiwari IBM nanocrystal memory (1996); SunRise quasi-volatile 3D NOR; Phase B N-10 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Qualifying one gain-cell macro across U.S. logic flows makes on-die MB-scale memory a standard block, trimming off-chip DRAM demand for caches and KV buffers.
killer_doubt: At ~0.03 um2/bit a GB needs ~300 mm2 of a ~$25k logic wafer, ~$100-150/GB against ~$20/GB contract DRAM. Foundries will not open their 18A or N4 PDKs.
decisive_experiment: Port an OpenRAM-style 2T gain-cell macro to SKY130 and GF 22FDX MPWs. Measure retention, refresh power and bits/mm2 at 85 C, then publish the cost per MB against SRAM and HBM. ~$250k.
prior_art: OpenRAM on SKY130 (UCSC); Bar-Ilan/EPFL Si gain cells; imec IGZO 2T0C BEOL; SEL NOSRAM; R07 I-01411 (DROP) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Spin-on cyclopentasilane plus ns-laser crystallization makes a ~$5-10/wafer silicon tier with no epitaxy or layer transfer. It is a genuinely cheap semiconductor tier.
killer_doubt: Laser-crystallized poly-Si TFTs leak ~1e-13 A/um, so a 1 fF gain-cell node lasts ~1-10 ms. IGZO leaks aA-level at equally low temperature. Laser heat damages the tiers below.
decisive_experiment: In a glovebox, spin cyclopentasilane and ELA-crystallize 20 nm films, then build 2T gain cells. Measure off-current and 85 C retention, plus damage to underlying tiers after stacking 3. ~$250k.
prior_art: Kovio printed-Si RFID (closed 2014); Shimoda et al., Nature 2006 (Seiko Epson/JSR) solution-processed Si TFTs; Phase B N-37/N-38 oxide tiers [training knowledge].
